sentences.text: This Criminal Original Petition has been filed to call for the records in C.C. No.324 of 2009 on the file of the Judicial Magistrate Court No.II, Tiruppur and quash the proceedings initiated against the petitioners as abuse of process of Court.

2 The factual matrix of the case is as under:
2.1
The first petitioner is a retail seller/vendor at Tiruppur and the second petitioner is a company manufacturing coffee powder.
While so, the respondent, viz., the Food Inspector, visited the premises of the first petitioner and lifted samples of coffee powder on 09.01.2008 and sent the same to the Public Analyst.

The Public Analyst found certain deficiencies in the analysed sample and the opinion of the Public S. Hariharan vs The Food Inspector on 2 November, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108044835/
1 Analyst in his report dated 06.02.2008 is as follows:
Opinion:
I am of the opinion that the sample is adulterated since the sample found to contain coffee husk which shall be free from this sample as per Appendix B to the PFA Rule,
1955.

entities.text: Public S. Hariharan vs The Food Inspector
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Also the sample is found to be misbranded since it is not labelled in accordance with the requirements of Section 2 (ix),(a),(e) and (k) of the PFA Act, 1954 and also Appendix/A.08.01 (3) of the PFA Rule, 1955.
2.2

Thereafter, the respondent filed a complaint before the Judicial Magistrate Court No.II,
Tiruppur, for offences under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 against Hariharan (A1),
M. Paulraj (A2) and Narasu's Coffee Company (A3) and the same was taken on file on 07.12.2009.

A copy of the report of the Public Analyst was served on the petitioners as contemplated under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, on 12.12.2009, giving liberty to them to dispute the same within ten days from the date of receipt thereof.
2.3 Be that as it may, the petitioners have challenged the entire prosecution on the short ground that the prosecution itself has been launched after the shelf life of the coffee powder.

3 Heard Mr. K.V. Sridharan, learned counsel for the petitioners and Mr.C.Emalias, learned Additional Public Prosecutor.
4

The learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that from the Public Analyst's report, it is evident that the coffee powder was manufactured and packed in January 2008 and that the packet carries a printing BEST BEFORE 4 MONTHS FROM PACKAGING.

Relying upon this, the learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the complaint should have been filed within four months from January 2008, whereas, admittedly, the complaint has been filed by the respondent only in 2009, which is after the shelf life of the coffee powder.

5 I am not inclined to persuade myself to agree with this submission of the learned counsel for the petitioners, because, the expression BEST BEFORE 4 MONTHS FROM PACKAGING does not mean that the shelf life of the coffee powder is only four months.
The said expression only means that coffee will have its best taste, flavour and aroma, if it is used within four months from the date of manufacturing of coffee powder and nothing more.
It is for the Analyst of the Central Food Laboratory to opine whether a product sent to them, had lost its flavour on account of lapse of time.
That apart, the petitioners are prosecuted for misbranding as well, for which, shelf life is not relevant at all.

P.N. PRAKASH, J.

sentences.text: In view of the above, this is not a fit case to quash the prosecution at the threshold.

Accordingly,
this Criminal Original Petition stands dismissed with liberty to the petitioners to raise all points before the Trial Court.

It is made clear that the observations made herein are only for the limited purpose of deciding this quash petition and the same shall not be, in any way, prejudicial to the rights of the petitioners before the Trial Court.
Connected M.P. is closed.
